The present Bail Application has been filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) on behalf of the Petitioner, Saurav Kumar, seeking the grant of anticipatory Bail in connection with FIR No. 776/2024 registered at P.S. Palam Village for offences punishable under Sections 420/120B/34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
2.
Briefly stated, the Petitioner started his business venture Future Flyers Group  at Palam Extension in the year 2019 and the institute was growing till Covid-19 engulfed the society at large.

sentences.text:
The Petitioner was engaged in providing integrated Commercial Pilot Licence Programme as per DGCA guidelines and the same included CPL/ATPL ground subject training as per DGCA, RTR (A)
exam preparations as per WPC standards and pilot training school.
4. The Complainant/Ankush Singh enrolled himself in RTR and CPL classes with the institute on 14.06.2019.

The complainant paid a total sum of Rs. 4 lacs to the Petitioner which included not only coaching fees for the ground classes training, but also certain portion of the fees was for certain paper fee and assisting the Complainant in filling up various scholarship forms and guiding to through the process.
5. The Complainant/Vicky Anand enrolled himself in RTR and CPL classes with the institute on 19.09.2019 and paid a total sum of Rs. 3.20 lacs to the Petitioner.
6. The Complainant/ Deepak Narwade enrolled himself in CPL classes with the institute on 22.06.2020 and paid a total sum of Rs. 1.5 lacs to the Petitioner.

7. It is submitted that since he could not run his business during COVID and his pending bills were mounting higher, despite the entire coaching classes being shifted to virtual mode, he was compelled to close down his outlet in Dwarka and ran his institute though virtual mode and through the physical set up in Bihar.

8. It is submitted that a few students started creating ruckus and after the pandemic period got over,
some student in a planned manner started leveling allegations against the Petitioner.

The FIR was registered on 24.12.2024 based on the Complaint of Ankush Singh, Vicky Anand,
and Deepak Narwade.

10. Though on account of the growing tension the Petitioner on 25.12.2021 showing his bona fide,
emailed Complainant/Deepak Narwarde explaining the break-up of the fees and offering to return the balance fee for which services could not be offered due to certain unforeseen circumstances.
11. The Complainant/Deepak Narwarde, after a series of email exchanges, agreed to the proposal on 28.03.2022.

Subsequently, during Anticipatory Bail proceedings before the Ld. ASJ vide order dated 23.06.2025 granted interim protection to the Petitioner as the complainants namely Vicky Anand and Ankush Singh requested for settlement.

The matter before the mediation centre on 04.07.2025.
12.
The Applicant joined mediation proceedings on 04.07.2025, 05.07.2025, and 07.07.2025, but the same failed due to unrealistic demands.
The Ld. Special Judge dismissing the Application had refused to grant Anticipatory Bail to the Petitioner vide order dated 11.07.2025.

sentences.text: The Anticipatory Bail is sought on the grounds that the instant FIR is ill motivated and is a deliberate attempt to harass the Petitioner unnecessarily, and the FIR is a result of the failure of the Complainant's in securing scholarship and that there has been no actual crime that was perpetrated.
No overt act has been attributed to the Petitioner.

14. It is submitted that the entire matter is based on documentary evidence and that nothing is to be recovered from the Petitioner and there is a delay of almost 5 years in registering the present FIR from the date of the alleged incident.
15. Regarding the Section 41A Cr.P.C. notice served for 19.05.2025, it is This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 04/12/2025 at 21:54:35 submitted that the Petitioner was in Patna, Bihar, and could not arrange travel on such short notice but is now willing to join the investigation.
16.

It is further submitted that the entire case relies on banking transactions and documentary evidence which are already in the possession of the Investigating Officer (IO), rendering custodial interrogation unnecessary.

17. The Ld. Counsel for the Applicant has placed reliance on Shailesh Kumar Singh alia Shailesh R.
Singh vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors., 2025 INSC 869, Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others vs. State of Punjab (1980) 2 SCC 565, Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar and Anr. (2014) 8 SCC 273, Sharad Kumar Aggarwal vs. State (2012) 194 DLT 489, Tejinder Pal Singh vs. State of NCT of Delhi; in Bail Appl. No. 2121/2025 and Anukul Singh vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr., 2025 INSC 1153.

sentences.text: Thus, it is prayed that the Anticipatory Bail be granted.
19. The status report has been filed on behalf of the State.

The Applicant allegedly induced multiple students and received money in his personal bank account without fulfilling the promised scholarships under the "Eduaide Foundation".
20.

The Applicant vacated the office premises at Ramphal Chowk, Dwarka, and was not found there during an inquiry on 21.04.2025.
21.
It is submitted that the Custodial interrogation is claimed to be necessary to recover the cheated amount and trace the money trail.

22. The Ld. APP for the Stated has vehemently opposed the Bail Application on the grounds that a Notice under Section 41A Cr.P.C. was served on the Applicant at his permanent address in Munger,
Bihar on 15.05.2025, but he failed to join the investigation.

Further, the role and identity of the accused is clearly mentioned in the FIR.
24. It is submitted that custodial interrogation is necessary to unearth the larger conspiracy, verify money trails, and identify any other co-accused persons or victims.
25. Thus, it is prayed that the Application be dismissed.
Submissions Heard and Record Perused.
26. While the allegations involve Section 420 IPC, the core of the dispute appears to stem from a contract for educational services that could not be fully fulfilled, allegedly due to the pandemic.
The distinction between a mere breach of contract and the offence of cheating, is a matter of trial.

The email correspondence placed on record prima facie suggests that there was communication regarding refunds, which dilutes the apprehension that the Petitioner fled with criminal intent at the very outset.
27. The case rests primarily on documentary evidence regarding fee transfers and promises made via brochures or emails.
The identity of the accused is established, and the Bank Accounts into which money was transferred, can be scrutinized without the necessity of pretrial incarceration.

As held by the Apex Court in Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694,
arrest should be the last option and restricted to exceptional cases.

sentences.text: 28. The Applicant's failure to join the investigation on one occasion i.e. on 19.05.2025, pursuant to the Notice under Section 41A has been explained by his counsel as being due to his presence in Bihar and the Notice being short.
This single instance of non-appearance, given the explanation, does not justify the denial of Bail.

It is noted that the Applicant did participate in Mediation Proceedings, which indicates a willingness to resolve the dispute, even though the mediation eventually did not succeed.
30. In view of the facts and circumstances, and this Court is of the opinion that the Applicant has made out a case for the grant of Anticipatory Bail.

31. Accordingly, it is directed that in the event of arrest, the Applicant/Saurav Kumar, be released on Bail in connection with FIR No. 776/2024, PS Palam Village, subject to the following conditions:

sentences.text: (i) The Applicant shall furnish a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one Surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer/Arresting Officer.

(ii) The Applicant shall join the investigations, as and when called by the Investigating Officer and shall co-operate during the investigations.
(iii) The Applicant shall furnish his cellphone number to the Investigating Officer on which he may be contacted at any time and shall ensure that the number is kept active and switched-on at all times.
(iv) The Applicant shall not contact, nor visit, nor offer any inducement, threat or promise to any of the prosecution witnesses or other persons acquainted with the facts of case.
(v) The Applicant shall not tamper with evidence nor otherwise indulge in any act or omission that is unlawful or that would prejudice the proceedings in the pending trial.
32. The Anticipatory Bail Application is allowed in the aforesaid terms.

NEENA BANSAL KRISHNA, J.
